narration: You've been told that if you get just one percent better every day, you'll end the year thirty-seven times better. It's the most famous promise in this whole book. So here's the question nobody stops to ask.
If that were actually true, why doesn't a single person you know end the year thirty-seven times better at anything at all?
Because that thirty-seven isn't a discovery about people. It's one point oh one, raised to the three hundred sixty-fifth power. A calculator made that number. Not a study.
And yet. Strip the fake number off the top, and the real idea survives. Small choices are never neutral. You're compounding up, or down, every single day.
But the book's sharpest idea isn't the math at all. It's this. You don't need to want the result more. You need to become the kind of person for whom that result is just what happens.
That idea holds up. The thirty-seven doesn't. The full honest verdict is on the channel.
